topic: One District One Product (ODOP) Scheme of Uttar Pradesh
description: The One District One Product (ODOP) scheme by the Government of Uttar Pradesh is a flagship initiative aimed at encouraging indigenous and specialized products of the state. It focuses on preserving traditional crafts, boosting local economies, and generating mass employment at the district level.

sections.title: Introduction and Launch of the Scheme
sections.description: Basic concept of the scheme and important facts related to its inception.

key_concepts.explanation: Operated by the Department of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), this scheme strives to bring global recognition to the unique traditional products belonging to all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh.

historical_events.significance: The scheme was officially launched by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on the occasion of Uttar Pradesh Day (UP Diwas).

important_facts.fact: The ODOP Scheme of Uttar Pradesh is originally inspired by the successful 'One Village One Product' (OVOP) initiative of Japan.
Renowned Bollywood actress Kangana Ranaut was appointed as the brand ambassador for the UP ODOP scheme.

sections.title: Products of Western Uttar Pradesh
sections.description: A list of major districts in Western UP and their designated ODOP products.

key_associations.extra_info: Highly famous for the manufacturing and export of footwear and other leather goods.
Popularly known across the country as 'Lock City' (Tala Nagari).
Globally renowned as 'Brass City' (Peetal Nagari) for its intricate brassware.
Famous as 'Suhag Nagari', specifically known for manufacturing glass bangles.
A major hub for the production of high-quality cricket bats and other sports equipment.
Famous for its intricately carved wooden handicrafts and premium furniture.
The Noida region serves as a massive manufacturing hub for apparel and textiles.

sections.title: Products of Central UP and Bundelkhand
sections.description: Crucial ODOP items belonging to the Awadh and Bundelkhand regions of the state.

key_associations.extra_info: Traditional and delicate thread embroidery that has been popular since the era of the Nawabs.
Recognized globally and referred to as the 'Perfume Capital of India'.
Involves carving beautiful statues and decorative items out of a soft, white-colored stone.
Known for the large-scale manufacturing of stuffed toys made from cloth and cotton.
Designated as ODOP due to the abundant production of high-quality sugarcane in these regions.
Traditional flat-woven floor coverings made primarily from cotton yarn.

sections.title: Products of Eastern UP / Purvanchal
sections.description: Culturally significant products associated with the districts of Eastern Uttar Pradesh.

key_associations.extra_info: World-famous for its luxurious silk and intricate gold and silver brocade or Zari work.
Involves creating statues and decorative artifacts from baked clay; this craft also holds a GI tag.
Eco-friendly baskets and handicrafts woven from a local wild grass known as 'Moonj'.
Known as 'Carpet City', it is the largest hand-knotted carpet weaving industry hub in South Asia.
A premium scented rice variety, historically referred to as 'Lord Buddha's Gift' (Buddha ka Mahaprasad).
The Nizamabad region of Azamgarh is famous for its unique and shiny black clay artifacts with silver engravings.

sections.title: Other Important Districts and Products
sections.description: A collection of frequently asked ODOP mappings from various other crucial districts.

key_associations.extra_info: Pratapgarh is one of the largest producers of Indian gooseberry in the country.
A major processing hub for this pungent spice widely used in Indian cuisine.
Accounts for the majority of the handcrafted bamboo flutes manufactured in India.
A traditional cottage industry focused on crafting Dholaks using locally sourced wood and animal hide.
The Khurja town within this district is historically famous for its glazed ceramic pottery.
A unique and intricate art form that involves inlaying fine brass wire into dark wood.

important_facts.fact: To boost the global sales, marketing, and reach of ODOP products, the UP Government has signed Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with e-commerce giants like Amazon and Flipkart.
